info.title: Maskin Dev Workspace API
info.description: Unified API for insights, bets, tasks, actors, and automation

agent_actor_id.description: Actor id of the agent to call. Must be an agent that is a workspace member.

conversation_id.description: The chat the call is started from. When the caller is a participant of it, the agent is given its recent messages and the transcript is saved into it. Ignored otherwise.

sdp.description: The SDP answer to set as the remote description.

tools_available.description: False when the server could not attach its tool connection to the call. The browser then answers every tool call with an "unavailable" result so the agent says so.

reason.description: Why the browser is ending the call. user_hangup for End call / Esc / close; network_error when the one ICE restart did not recover the connection.

input_audio_seconds.description: Seconds of microphone audio the client sent. Clamped to the call length.

output_audio_seconds.description: Seconds of agent audio the client received. Clamped to the call length.

audio.description: Base64 of a WAV file (16 kHz mono recommended).

get.summary: Get object with relationships and connected objects
Bounded multi-hop graph traversal from an object
get.description: Breadth-first walk from the given object across `relationships`, bounded by `max_depth`, `max_nodes`, and an optional `edge_types` allow-list. Visited set keyed on object id, so cyclic edges (e.g. `supersedes` loops) terminate. Only object endpoints inside the caller's workspace are followed — file endpoints and cross-workspace ids are skipped.

200.description: Bounded subgraph reachable from the start object

get.description: Returns the composed workspace briefing (active bets, closed bets, loops, open insights, recent learnings) as a markdown string. Same document agents receive at session start.

post.summary: Generate today's brief as spoken prose
post.description:
The human-facing brief: the workspace's default agent (its Chief of Staff) writing the same facts as something to listen to, rather than the agent-facing markdown `GET /briefing` returns.

POST because it generates — one small model call, on demand, only when someone asks to hear it. The result is cached for the rest of the UTC day under a fingerprint of the workspace state, so asking again costs nothing unless something actually changed. Falls back to deterministic prose when the workspace has no chat-callable credentials, so this never fails for want of a model.

get.summary: List loops in workspace with derived stats
get.description: Returns every Loop object in the workspace with per-row derived fields (in-progress / closed counts, median close time, agent-actor ids, per-viewer waiting flag) computed from a single request. Returns an empty array — not an error — for workspaces with zero loops. Pass `id` to scope to a single loop (still returns `{loops: [...]}`, empty array if that id is not a loop in this workspace).

schema.description: Scope the result to a single loop id (used by get_loop). Omit to list every loop in the workspace.

get.summary: Agent-work events (session + trigger) scoped to a loop's triggers
get.description: Returns the loop's agent-work event feed: `trigger_fired` events for the trigger ids listed in the loop's `metadata.trigger_ids`, plus `session_*` lifecycle events for sessions launched from those triggers. Newest first. Returns `{ events: [] }` — not an error — for a loop with no triggers, no fired triggers, or an unknown id (a foreign loop returns empty without leaking existence).

200.description: Agent-work events for this loop, newest first

400.description: Missing workspace ID or malformed loop id

get.summary: Vertical-story step spine for one loop
get.description: Returns the loop's ordered step spine — one row per trigger id in `metadata.trigger_ids`, with hands-off / escalates fields and per-viewer waiting-on-viewer counts pre-resolved so the vertical-story renderer can spread it as-is. Empty array for a loop with no triggers or an unknown id.

post.summary: Reconcile DB sessions against an agent-server sandbox snapshot

post.summary: Create a comment on an object

entity_id.description: Object ID to post the comment on.

content.description: Keep it short: lead with the point, keep only what changes the reader's decision, plain words, and never use the long dash (em dash). Write it like a Slack message, not a report: one thought per comment, plain conversational language, direct. No headers, no bold labels, no bulleted sections, no walls of text. When referencing another object in human-facing text, use a markdown link `[title](link)` — never paste partial UUIDs. Hard limit: 50000 characters — the API rejects anything over the limit with a validation error. You can embed an inline chart by writing a fenced ```chart block whose body is a JSON spec — `{ "type": "bar" | "line" | "area", "x": "<x-field>", "series": ["<series1>", ...], "data": [{ "<x-field>": ..., "<series1>": <number>, ... }], "caption": "optional short label" }`. The UI renders it as a bounded-height recharts visual; malformed specs degrade to a small "couldn't render chart" note without breaking the comment.

mentions.description: Array of actor UUIDs. For each @mentioned agent actor, the server creates a needs_input notification AND spawns a session that lets the agent read the comment and reply on the same object. @mention human actors whenever you need their input, decision, or attention: they get a notification about the comment, so this is the right way to pull a human into the loop. Don't mention humans gratuitously, but don't hesitate to mention them when their input would actually unblock you. Every id must come from a live list_actors call — never retype a UUID from memory, from your system prompt, or from an earlier message, because a single wrong character silently mentions nobody. Ids that match no actor are dropped and reported back in the response's `unresolved_mentions`; if you see that field, look the actor up with list_actors and post a follow-up comment with the corrected mention.

parent_event_id.description: Set this to thread a reply under an existing comment (use the id returned by get_comments). If a thought is long, split it into multiple short comments or use parent_event_id to thread a reply instead of one long comment.

attachment_file_ids.description: First upload files with create_file (or pick existing ones with list_files) and pass the returned file ids here (max 10). Attached files appear as clickable cards under the posted comment.

metadata.description: To surface a live task checklist, pass { tasks: ["<task-uuid>", ...] } — each row renders as a checkbox (checked iff the task's status is done/completed/succeeded), a link to the task, and its driver avatar, and updates automatically when the referenced task changes. This field does not carry options for the human to pick from: asking for a call is what `decision` is for, and it is the only way to do it.

title.description: 3-7 words. The decision itself, not a status. A question if it is a judgment call ("Is the onboarding bet worth running?"), a noun phrase if it is an artifact ("Acme's note before Thursday"). No agent name, and no verb-ing: "Reviewing the funnel" is a status, not a decision.

summary.description: 1-2 sentences. Sentence 1: the state of the world and the cost of the status quo, with one real number you actually looked up. Sentence 2: what is already done, so the human knows they are only deciding, not working. Never restate the title.

ask.description: First person, one sentence. Name the single call you cannot make alone and why it belongs to the human: "Notices go to real households, so I will not send this alone." No hedging, no apologising, no offering to help.

label.description: 4 words or fewer, sentence case. The choice itself: "7-day window", "Hold", "Ship to 10%". Not a sentence, and not a verb phrase describing what you will do.

consequences.description: 2-3 lines, present tense, one clause each: "Ships with cycle 1 tomorrow", "Adds 18 support tickets in week one". Make one of them the downside, because an option with only upsides is not a real choice (the API does not check this one; the human will). Where numbers trade off, give both sides with units. No semicolons and no ", and" — that is two lines, not one.

recommended.description: Set true on exactly one option, the one you would take. Recommending nothing pushes the whole call back onto the human; recommending everything says nothing.

destructive.description: Set true on an option that cannot be undone or that reaches real people (sends, deletes, spends, ships). The human is asked to confirm it before it goes out, and it never fires from a lock-screen button alone. Leave it off for reversible choices.

options.description: 2 or 3 options, exactly one marked recommended. These render as the buttons the human taps, so they must be the real choices rather than yes/no/maybe.

id.description: Only in `drafts`: a short key for this message ("kenneth", "dan-1"), unique within the card. Taking an action on the message replies with it, so you can tell which message was sent or skipped.

object_id.description: The object whose description IS the draft, and nothing else (a task or content object the draft is saved on). The card shows its current description, live, so a later edit shows up. Prefer this: do not copy the text.

file_id.description: The workspace file the card is about, when what you are asking about is a file and not text to send: an HTML page, a markdown document, an image, a plain-text file. The card shows the file itself (a rendered page, the formatted text, the picture) above the buttons, live, so a later version shows up. Save the file first (create_file), then give its id. Use object_id instead for a message that would be sent.

label.description: What kind of text it is, shown as a small label above it: "Email to Hans", "LinkedIn note", "Slack message". Plain words, at most 30 characters. Defaults to "Draft" (or the file name for a file).

to.description: Who it goes to, as a person would read it: "Hans Jensen, Netwerk". Leave out for a public post.

body.description: Only when the draft is not saved as an object: the exact text you will send, character for character, in the language it will be sent in. Not a summary. Ignored in favour of the object description when object_id is set and the object has one.

drafts.description: Use this instead of `draft` when one card asks about several messages (up to 10), for example five first DMs. Each message shows as its own preview with its own Send and Skip, and the human's tap on one replies to you as "Send: <label> to <to> (<id>)" or "Skip: ...". Give every message an `id`. The card's options still apply to the whole batch. Never put the text in the summary.

id.description: Only in `drafts`: a short key for this message ("kenneth", "dan-1"), unique within the card. Taking an action on the message replies with it, so you can tell which message was sent or skipped.

object_id.description: The object whose description IS the draft, and nothing else (a task or content object the draft is saved on). The card shows its current description, live, so a later edit shows up. Prefer this: do not copy the text.

file_id.description: The workspace file the card is about, when what you are asking about is a file and not text to send: an HTML page, a markdown document, an image, a plain-text file. The card shows the file itself (a rendered page, the formatted text, the picture) above the buttons, live, so a later version shows up. Save the file first (create_file), then give its id. Use object_id instead for a message that would be sent.

label.description: What kind of text it is, shown as a small label above it: "Email to Hans", "LinkedIn note", "Slack message". Plain words, at most 30 characters. Defaults to "Draft" (or the file name for a file).

to.description: Who it goes to, as a person would read it: "Hans Jensen, Netwerk". Leave out for a public post.

body.description: Only when the draft is not saved as an object: the exact text you will send, character for character, in the language it will be sent in. Not a summary. Ignored in favour of the object description when object_id is set and the object has one.

draft.description: Attach this whenever the call is whether to send something in a person's name or to the outside world (an email, a message, a post). The card shows the draft above the buttons, so the human reads exactly what would go out. Without it they are approving a message they cannot see. Point at the object that holds the draft with object_id (preferred), or give the exact text as body. When the card is about a file instead (an HTML page, a markdown document, an image), give file_id and the card shows the file itself. Never put the text in the summary.

decision.description:
Attach this when you need a human to make a call, together with that human in `mentions` — a decision with an empty `mentions` array reaches nobody.
It renders as a card in their For You feed: the title is the headline, the summary and ask are the body, and each option becomes a button. If the call is whether to send something, attach `draft` (the object that holds it, or the exact text) and it shows above the buttons.

The API checks the rules below and rejects a decision that breaks any of them, listing every violation at once:
title 3-7 words and not opening with a status verb ("Reviewing the funnel"); summary at most 2 sentences, carrying at least one digit, and not a restatement of the title;
ask exactly one sentence, first person; 2-3 options with exactly one marked recommended, each label 4 words or fewer;
2-3 consequence lines per option, one clause each (no semicolons, no ", and"); and nowhere in the block an em-dash, an en-dash, an emoji,
or a hedge word standing in for a number ("significantly", "substantially", "several", "many", and the like).

The rest is house style the API does not check. Write to it anyway, because a human reads the result:
sentence case, uppercase only for micro-labels; cut every adjective that is not load-bearing; no metadiscourse,
and no summarising what the human can already see on screen. If you can delete a word and the decision is still clear, delete it.

Example:
{ "title": "Is the onboarding bet worth running?",
  "summary": "3 of 5 signups stall on step 2, costing about 40 activations a week. I have drafted the replacement copy and the migration.",
  "ask": "This changes what every new customer sees first, so I will not ship it alone.",
  "options": [
    { "label": "7-day window", "recommended": true, "consequences": ["Ships with cycle 1 tomorrow", "Adds 18 support tickets in week one"] },
    { "label": "Hold", "consequences": ["Nothing ships this cycle", "Keeps losing 40 activations a week"] } ] }

attention.description:
How important and urgent this comment is for the human reading it, on a 1-5 scale. Score it yourself, from the human's point of view — this drives the ordering of their For You feed, so score consistently rather than defaulting to the middle every time:
5 = Critical — blocks progress right now or needs an urgent human decision (e.g. something is broken, a deadline/money is at risk, an approval is blocking work).
4 = High — an important decision or blocker coming up that the human should look at today, but it isn't on fire.
3 = Normal — a noteworthy update, finding, or question; worth a look when convenient, no rush.
2 = Low — a minor note, context, or non-blocking observation.
1 = FYI — nice to know, purely informational, no action expected.
Leave unset if you genuinely can't judge urgency; an unset score sorts below any scored comment. Reserve 5 for things that are genuinely business-critical — inflating scores buries the comments that actually need it.

post.summary: Start a 1:1 voice call: reserve the caller’s live-call slot
post.description: Any agent in the workspace can be called: the agent's own voice_enabled field is not checked. Body: { agent_actor_id, conversation_id? }. On success, inserts a voice_sessions row (status=pending) and returns its id. The browser then posts its WebRTC offer to POST /voice-sessions/{id}/offer. No credential is returned: the connection to the vendor is made by the server.

400.description: Target actor is not an agent

404.description: Flag off, or target agent not found in caller workspace

409.description: Caller already has a live voice session

500.description: The reservation row could not be written

post.summary: Connect a reserved voice session to the vendor
post.description: Only the human who reserved the session, still a member of its workspace, can call this; anyone else gets 404. Accepts one offer per session. The server posts the SDP offer and the session config (instructions, tools, transcription) to the vendor with the operator key, attaches its own tool connection to the new call, and returns the SDP answer. During the call, tools that only read run at once; every other tool is held until the person says yes out loud. The browser never receives a vendor credential.

404.description: Flag off, no such session for the caller, or membership lapsed

409.description: The session already took an offer, or is no longer pending

429.description: Rate limited by the vendor; retry after `retry_after_seconds`

500.description: Voice is not configured (no operator key), the vendor connect failed, or the vendor refused it over quota or billing (message says the team has been notified) — the session row is released so the caller can start again

post.summary: End a voice call
post.description: Marks the caller's voice_sessions row ended, stamps ended_at and ended_reason, finalises audio seconds and total_cost_usd, and fires voice_session_ended. Idempotent: hanging up a call that already ended returns its stored terminal state and fires nothing.

404.description: Flag off, or no such voice session for the caller

post.summary: Transcribe a short voice recording (chat dictation)
post.description: Sends the audio to a speech-to-text model on OpenRouter (default Voxtral Small, override with MASKIN_TRANSCRIPTION_MODEL) and returns the text. Requires X-Workspace-Id; the call is billed to the operator account, so a read-only viewer is refused.

200.description: Transcript; empty text when no speech was detected

429.description: The speech provider is rate limiting us

500.description: Transcription is not configured on this server
